CI vcpkg binary cache

ci-tests.yml and vcpkg-binary-cache.yml share .github/scripts/vcpkg_cache_contract.py, schema v5. Both restore and save exactly .vcpkg-cache/binary (including the same slash spelling on Windows). Actions cache versions also depend on paths and compression; identical key text alone does not make different path lists compatible. Downloads retain their separate v3 cache. Installer workflows keep their existing independent contracts.

Only ABI-addressed ZIP archives are cached by these two workflows. Installed and packages trees are reconstructed by vcpkg on each fresh runner, so cached installed state cannot bypass its binary ABI decisions. No ABI overrides, compiler hash suppression, package renaming, or SDK metadata rewriting are used.

The key prefix includes OS, architecture, triplet, runtime boundary, tool identity, vcpkg baseline, and the existing manifest/configuration hash. Linux runtime identity is distribution plus release (for example ubuntu-24.04 versus ubuntu-26.04). Compiler versions/target, glibc, linker, CMake and Ninja versions select a preferred snapshot. ImageVersion, dates and run IDs are excluded. Fallback first relaxes the manifest, then tools/baseline within the same runtime boundary; vcpkg still checks each archive's ABI. There is no fallback across Ubuntu releases or macOS SDK identities. Keep ubuntu-latest and windows-latest: migration creates a new runtime boundary without permanently freezing runners. macOS retains its existing hash of Xcode version and resolved SDK path and its SDK metadata guard.

Actions caches are immutable. The restore lookup ends in snapshot; saved keys instead contain a deterministic digest of archive names and contents. Repairs also include a digest of the restored key, so an older complete inventory can supersede a newer incomplete snapshot even if that inventory was saved previously. Prefix restore selects the newest matching snapshot. Thus a normal warm restore reports a fallback hit, even with identical environment and dependencies. After successful install, changed contents get a new key, including after an incomplete exact/fallback hit; unchanged contents skip saving. Empty snapshots are not saved. Bump SCHEMA for a contract change or an intentionally retired generation; do not introduce dates. Concurrent saves of identical contents can race harmlessly; check the cache action log for actual upload confirmation, not just its step outcome.

Remote NuGet configuration remains centralized. Test jobs request read, and only the main-only warming workflow requests readwrite with packages: write and an exact trusted SHA checkout. NuGet credentials remain under RUNNER_TEMP, outside cached paths and artifacts. Configuration validation proves local XML structure, not feed authorization or publication. PR cache writes remain isolated to their merge ref. Arbitrary source dispatches cannot save persistent vcpkg snapshots or downloads, using the existing trusted-source scope resolver.

Evidence and remaining uncertainty

CI run 41187027988, Windows job 124495961654, restored an exact v4 binary snapshot, restored 0 local and 0 NuGet packages, rebuilt dependencies (vcpkg reported 51 minutes), then skipped saving. NuGet returned package-specific NotFound URLs containing ABI versions. This demonstrates that the exact snapshot was insufficient, not that all remote caching is useless. The warming workflow at the audited revision used v3 mixed-tree caches on Windows, incompatible with the test job's v4 archive path and key. Linux used mixed installed trees with no release/tool identity.

The most recent manually dispatched warming run found during this audit, 30166602199, succeeded, but its job logs now return HTTP 410. Publication of the currently requested ABI versions could not be established. Linux job-log retrieval failed through the connector, and its telemetry artifact download returned HTTP 403. Linux remote restore latency therefore remains unmeasured in this audit. A package 404 can mean absence, an unpublished ABI, or hidden access restrictions; configuration success alone cannot distinguish these. Remote caching is retained pending measurements.

Cold/warm validation

  1. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/ci -p test_vcpkg_cache_contract.py. After merging, dispatch vcpkg Binary Cache on main, initially with bypass_local_compiled_cache=true. This prevents local snapshots from hiding remote behavior and seeds missing ABIs. Inspect the install log's NuGet upload reports and package versions in GitHub Packages. Existing installed packages or locally restored archives do not necessarily republish to NuGet.
  2. Dispatch the same main SHA again with bypass still true, on the same compatible environment. Compare environment summaries and representative .abi.json files. Require matching requested ABI package versions and successful NuGet read-back; successful setup or an upload report alone is insufficient. Summaries show NuGet restored counts and provider duration separately from full install duration. Investigate 401/403, package-specific 404s, and different compiler/ABI hashes before attributing zero hits or Linux latency to the cache backend.
  3. Dispatch warming with bypass false to publish a default-branch v5 Actions snapshot. On the new schema this is the cold local run. Repeat on the same compatible environment for the warm local run, then dispatch CI Debug Tests on main with profile pr (or release) to execute the existing CTest suites. Compare matched key, restored/rebuilt counts, install duration, and save action logs. A warm prefix hit and skipped unchanged-content save are expected. Record both durations; do not infer a speedup from cache-hit status alone.

A trusted main warming run is required to publish remote packages; main snapshots are reusable by PRs, while PR-scoped snapshots cannot seed main. If the runner or compiler changes between validation runs, compare identities and ABIs before calling the second run warm. Install logs/ABI files are retained with existing telemetry artifacts, including successful warming runs. Counts across retries are restore events and unique build-start package identifiers, not proof of remote publication. No post-change CI timings are claimed by this change.
